This case presents a well-delineated, developmentally contextualized behavioral profile consistent with Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD), mild severity, school-predominant presentation. The diagnosis is rigorously supported by DSM-5 criteria: (1) duration (>6 months), (2) specific symptom domains (angry/irritable mood + argumentative/defiant behavior), (3) functional impairment limited to school setting, (4) exclusion of alternative explanations (ADHD, anxiety, depression, conduct disorder), and (5) cross-informant confirmation (parent/teacher rating scales + structured interview). Critically, the *absence* of symptoms outside the ODD domain — including no inattention, hyperactivity, internalizing symptoms, or antisocial behaviors — strengthens diagnostic specificity. The school-predominant pattern, with preserved functioning at home, further aligns with empirically observed subtypes of ODD and argues against pervasive neurodevelopmental or mood disorders. No red flags suggest medical, neurological, or sensory contributors (e.g., no language delay, motor incoordination, sleep disturbance, or autonomic signs), and the summary explicitly states no medical workup is indicated — consistent with a purely behavioral, non-somatic presentation.

[EVIDENCE]  
• Persistent pattern (>6 months) of angry/irritable mood and argumentative/defiant behavior toward authority figures.  
• Symptoms confirmed via parent/teacher rating scales (Vanderbilt, SNAP-IV) and structured clinical interview.  
• Functional impairment evident as classroom disruption and refusal of directed activities.  
• No aggression toward people/animals, property destruction, deceitfulness, or serious rule violations — ruling out Conduct Disorder.  
• No reported symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, or impulsivity — ruling out ADHD.  
• No endorsed symptoms of anxiety (e.g., worry) or depression (e.g., sadness, anhedonia, sleep/appetite changes).  
• Appropriate mood and affect observed on mental status examination.  
• Contextual specificity: Behaviors predominantly occur at school; age-appropriate cooperation and prosocial behavior observed at home.  
• Symptoms are behaviorally and developmentally grounded — no indication for medical workup.

[GAPS]  
None.

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Oppositional Defiant Disorder, mild severity, school-predominant presentation
